newsitem.title: USA: SEC EDGAR processing hits snag.
newsitem.headline: SEC EDGAR processing hits snag.

text.p: Monday's successful restart of the Securities and Exchange Commission's main electronic filing computer was short-lived after problems developed in the key database, limiting public access in its public reference room branch terminals.

Despite snags in the system though, public access to the electronic filings were still available through commercial information providers and the SEC website www.sec.gov., the commission said in a statement.

Problems to the Electronic Data Gathering Analysis and Retrieval (EDGAR) main computer apparently stemmed from components of the system weakened or altered during the power failure that occured on March 21, SEC said.

A power failure to the main computer located in Alexandria, Va., resulted in a major system failure which precluded it from being able to receive, process or disseminate electronic filings on March 21.
